sources.locator: Liber iuratus Honorii XXXIV–XXXVIII; diplomatic Royal17Axlii ff39r–40r; electronic editor Joseph H. Peterson.
sources.bounded_findings: XXXV supplies a complete opaque formula beginning Megal, agal, iegal. Local families include saleht/salym/salmeht/sameht/saloht. XXXVI then supplies an ordinary petition containing an explicit insertion instruction and a conditional divine-vision version. XXXVII supplies another full opaque block, XXXVIII another configurable petition. Diplomatic Royal text and corrected composite text are distinct columns; do not pool spellings or silently remove editorial brackets. The editor identifies Sloane3854 as a fourteenth-century witness, but Royal dates/provenance and exact medieval equivalence of these clauses need separate verification. No native manuscript image inspected.

sources.locator: Ars notoria sections50–56, especially52–56; full Theos formula section10 printed p104–105.
sources.bounded_findings: Opaque incipits identify successive blocks; instructions alternate these with Latin prayers. Section52 requires a half-hour interval before the third part. Section56 explicitly denies that the Latin passages provide exhaustive wordwise exposition of the opaque oration. Electronic edition includes late Latin Agrippa printing and Turner1657 translation; introduction notes omissions and fluid transmission. These are not automatically verified medieval clauses. Complete Megal block is supplied through Liber iuratus XXXV, not silently reconstructed inside Ars notoria.

precise_production_constraint: Compose a whole ritual account as fixed opaque recitation blocks plus separately written performance instructions and petition slots. Altering the expressly configurable petition need not alter the opaque block. Conversely moving a cited block or its prescribed interval changes the performance sequence even if its tokens remain unchanged. Do not replace this with mere repeated-word detection.
finite_contrast: A word-for-word bilingual exposition requires lexical correspondences between each opaque token and adjoining ordinary prose. The source explicitly disclaims that relation and supplies ordinary-language petition insertion independently. Formula-plus-instruction is a meaningful whole-account function even when individual voces lack recoverable ordinary lexical meanings. This does not prove the voces were meaningless to all historical users.
limits: No rule generating each artificial word has been established; local form families alone are descriptive.
A mixture of formulas and prose is not evidence that Voynich implements the same mixture.
No implicit AND, divine name, invocation or numeral assigned to any Voynich form.
The relation between late Ars notoria clauses and medieval witnesses must be checked before using an early-fifteenth-century production claim.
A source-only classifier or another refrain count would not change the manuscript decision; none proposed.
